name: gguf-quant
desc: Free, open-source GUI to quantize and convert LLMs to GGUF on Windows — presets, batch queue, VRAM hints. 100 MB portable, offline, MIT.
features: ✅ **One-click quantize** — pick Q4_K_M, Q5_K_M, Q8_0 or any K-quant preset and convert a source model to GGUF
✅ **Batch queue** — line up several models and quants; the queue runs overnight with per-job logs
✅ **Size and VRAM preview** — estimated file size and required VRAM per quant before a single byte is written
✅ **Imatrix support** — optional importance matrix pass for better quality at aggressive quants
✅ **Format intake** — reads safetensors and PyTorch checkpoints with a built-in shard merger
✅ **Real progress** — tensor-level progress bars from the llama.cpp backend, not a fake spinner
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime and conversion tools bundled, portable, offline, MIT with SHA-256 releases
compare: | Feature | **gguf-quant** | llama-quantize CLI | LM Studio | HF converters |
| Price | **Free, MIT** | Free, OSS | Free | Free |
| GUI with quant presets | **Yes** | No | Partial | No |
| Batch queue with logs | **Yes** | Scripted | No | No |
| VRAM estimate per quant | **Yes** | No | No | No |
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Build from source | Installer | Web or script |
faqQ: how to quantize a model to GGUF on Windows?
faqA: The reference path is a Python environment plus a llama.cpp build, which loses an evening for anyone outside the ML shell. gguf-quant wraps the same backend in presets with size and VRAM estimates, so you choose a quant and watch tensor-level progress. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, fully offline.
s1: Dark workbench (#121417, cyan #22D3EE): source model card left, quant preset list center with size estimates, VRAM hint chip reading 8.2 GB at 8k context.
s2: Batch queue view: three models with per-quant output sizes, progress bars running in parallel, log tail showing tensor names converting.
s3: Settings: threads slider, imatrix file picker, output folder with shard naming pattern, success toast reading Q4_K_M written 4.1 GB.
